cases.title: FFI boundary change should trigger a contract-focused interop audit
cases.goal: Confirm interop-auditor focuses on ownership, lifetime, allocator, ABI, error translation, and thread-safety at cross-language boundaries.
cases.setup: Use fixture `tiny-ffi-boundary` and the frozen diff `ffi_boundary.patch`. The diff changes returned buffer ownership, allocator behavior, and callback threading assumptions across the boundary.
cases.prompt: Spawn interop-auditor to review this Python/C++ boundary for ownership, lifetime, ABI, allocator, error-model, and threading risks.
expected_output_shape: Boundary-contract framing rather than generic review prose.
Residual uncertainty is called out explicitly.
expected_validation_behavior: Should identify missing interop tests or unverified runtime assumptions when relevant.
pass_criteria: Calls out copy-vs-borrow and cleanup risks if present.
Focuses on the language boundary rather than app-level logic.
fail_signals: Misses obvious ownership or ABI hazards.

cases.title: Pure single-language business logic should not trigger interop auditing
cases.goal: Confirm interop-auditor is not routed to ordinary single-language logic.
cases.setup: Diff changes only pure Python request validation logic with no FFI or boundary layer.
cases.prompt: Review this pure Python validation refactor.
expected_safety_behavior: Should not be chosen as the primary specialist.
expected_validation_behavior: No interop-specific testing discussion is expected.
pass_criteria: The harness routes this away from interop-auditor.
fail_signals: Invents cross-language concerns where none exist.
